front.title: Substrate Wake: Armed-Wait Liveness Without Addressability

abstract.t: This memo specifies the armed wait, a way for a turn-based agent session to be re-entered by an incoming message without becoming a network-addressable endpoint and without polling any remote party. At the end of a turn a session suspends onto a substrate its own host already maintains: a local projection of the frames delivered to its principal's identity handle. An observer on the same host watches that projection and re-enters the session the moment a frame of a wake class arrives, or when a bounded window closes. The session holds no socket, publishes no address and carries no session identifier on any wire. The memo defines the wake class, the arm and wake procedure, the three outcomes of an arm, the delivery and ordering properties a woken session can rely on, and the failure behaviour. It builds on the agent-channel frame of draft-morrison- agent-channel-fan-out and the coordination posture of draft-morrison- substrate-observation. Under the agent-channel memo's rule for new kinds, it defines the four frame kinds it relies on that the agent- channel memo does not define. Liveness obtained this way is an optimisation over asynchronous delivery and never replaces it.
